about.title: About isshoni
about.lead: Watch your friends' screens together, on a server one of you runs.

trust.heading: Privacy and trust
trust.server: The server is trusted. Video and sound are encrypted on the way, but the server passes them on, so whoever runs it could see the streams.
trust.noRecording: There is no recording, and there are no hidden viewers: an admin who watches shows up in the viewer list like everyone else.
trust.stored: The server stores usernames and password hashes, your sign-ins with their last-seen time and IP address, invites, rooms, notification subscriptions, and a log of logins and admin actions that is pruned after 30 days.
trust.local: Window titles never leave your device. Friends see a share as a screen, a window or a tab.
trust.noTelemetry: No telemetry: the server reports nothing about you or itself to the isshoni project. The privacy page lists every connection the server makes.

conntest.intro: This checks whether video can travel between this device and the server, the same way it does in a room.
conntest.running: Testing your connection… This takes up to 10 seconds.
conntest.udpDisabled: UDP media is turned off in the server config (listen.ice_udp).

status.amber: Works, but video may stutter on weak networks.

conntest.incomplete: Couldn't finish the test. Try again in a minute.
conntest.incompleteWait_one: Couldn't finish the test. Try again in {{count}} second.
conntest.incompleteWait_other: Couldn't finish the test. Try again in {{count}} seconds.
conntest.noPublicIp: The server doesn't know its public address, so browsers can't reach its media ports. Set public_ip in /etc/isshoni/isshoni.toml (Docker: ISSHONI_PUBLIC_IP in .env) and restart.

nat.none: This server has its public address on its own network interface, so no router or NAT is in the way.
nat.one_to_one: This server is behind 1:1 NAT (a cloud network or a container). Open the ports in the provider's firewall. In a container, also publish them. At home, also forward TCP 80, 443, {{tcpPort}} and UDP {{udpPort}} on your router to this machine.
nat.port_forward: Forward TCP 80, 443, {{tcpPort}} and UDP {{udpPort}} on your router to this machine.
nat.symmetric: This server has no public address; isshoni needs one (a VPS or a router port forward).
nat.cgnat_likely: This server has no public address; isshoni needs one (a VPS or a router port forward).
nat.unknown: isshoni couldn't tell how this server reaches the internet. Run isshoni doctor on the server for details.

conntest.ownNetwork: You may be testing from the server's own network. Test again from your phone's mobile data.
conntest.docker: Check that compose publishes {{udpPort}}:{{udpPort}}/udp; published ports bypass ufw.
conntest.macLocalNetwork: On a Mac, allow your browser Local Network access (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network).
conntest.blockedNetwork: If this network blocks UDP (some offices and hotels do), test from home or from your phone's mobile data.

firewall.aws: In the AWS console, add inbound rules to this instance's security group: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.gcp: In the Google Cloud console, add a VPC firewall rule that allows incoming UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.azure: In the Azure portal, add inbound rules to this VM's network security group: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.oracle: In the Oracle Cloud console, add ingress rules to the subnet's security list: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates. Oracle's images also block these ports with their own iptables rules, so open them on the server too.
firewall.hetzner: In the Hetzner Cloud console, check the Cloud Firewall attached to this server: allow incoming UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.digitalocean: In the DigitalOcean control panel, check the Cloud Firewall assigned to this Droplet: allow incoming UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.vultr: In the Vultr customer portal, check the Cloud Firewall group linked to this instance: allow incoming UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.linode: In Akamai Cloud Manager, check the Cloud Firewall attached to this Linode: allow incoming UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.scaleway: In the Scaleway console, add inbound rules to this instance's security group: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.ovh: In the OVHcloud control panel, add inbound rules to this instance's security group: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.alibaba: In the Alibaba Cloud console, add inbound rules to this instance's security group: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.tencent: In the Tencent Cloud console, add inbound rules to this instance's security group: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
firewall.unknown: Open these ports in your provider's firewall or security group: UDP {{udpPort}}, TCP 443 and {{tcpPort}}, and TCP 80 for certificates.
